{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUjYZpM8AAAABUGv_lQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlJVizg9odUo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlJVi", "number": 63, "title": "Guide repository-side GitHub Actions setup for label-driven continuous execution", "body": "## Problem

ProjectWeave's README, CLI usage guide, and `init-project` report currently tell operators to add Issues to a GitHub Project and manually set `AI execution = Ready` and `Status = Todo`. They do not explain how to configure repository-side GitHub Actions that synchronize Issue labels with Project membership and execution permission for continuous operation.

The shared ProjectWeave + GitWeave setup uses one Project for two repositories. GitHub's built-in auto-add workflow limit can prevent covering every repository. Operators need a documented optional Actions setup after Project initialization, with a clear account of which setup is performed by ProjectWeave and which setup remains external.

## Expected outcome

Update the README's getting-started section, `docs/usage.md`, and `init-project`'s post-initialization guidance to recommend and explain optional repository-side GitHub Actions for label-driven continuous execution. Keep manual onboarding available and make the choice clear without changing runtime selection policy.

Document this policy:

| Issue condition / event | Project behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Open, `task` label present, `draft` absent | Ensure Project membership and set `AI execution = Ready` automatically. |
| New eligible Project item, or eligible item with unset Status | Initialize Status to `Todo`. |
| Eligible item with an existing Status | Preserve that Status; never reset `In Progress` or `Done` to `Todo`. |
| `task` removed, `draft` added, or Issue closed | For existing Project items, set `AI execution = Not ready` and retain membership. Do not add ineligible Issues merely to update fields. |
| Issue closed | GitHub's built-in Issue-closed workflow sets `Done`; explain verifying it is enabled. The Issue close reason distinguishes completed work from not-planned work. |
| Issue becomes eligible again | Automatically restore `Ready`, preserving already-set Status. |

Explain that ProjectWeave does not itself set Ready: `coordinate` continuously selects open, Todo, Ready Issues subject to the configured resource policy. Actions synchronizes Project metadata and does not invoke AI. No Pending Status is needed. Changing to Not ready does not stop an already-running execution; cancellation and pre-merge eligibility gates are deferred work.

## Setup guidance

- Configure the workflow separately in every repository to be tracked; one Project can span multiple repositories.
- Ensure `task` and `draft` labels exist in each repository. Explain event handling for opened, reopened, closed, labeled, and unlabeled Issues, including removing draft.
- Explain required Project access and an expiring PAT in a repository Actions secret such as `ADD_TO_PROJECT_PAT`; ordinary `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot access Projects. Provide supported user/organization authentication guidance without exposing or repurposing existing credentials.
- Explain adding the workflow to each repository's default branch, provisioning secrets, verifying Project fields and the Issue-closed workflow, and performing a small live verification before continuous operation.
- Present Actions as an optional alternative to manual onboarding / built-in auto-add, including the built-in workflow-count limit. Verify current limits and authentication details against official GitHub documentation.
- Provide actionable post-init guidance pointing to the usage guide. Clearly state that init does not install repository workflows, create labels, provision secrets, or mark Issues Ready.
- Use reusable examples with owner, Project number, and repository configuration rather than requiring the dogfooding Project #4. Coordinate references to the automation documented by the implementation tasks below; do not advertise undeployed repository automation as already working.

## Scope and related work

This Issue covers onboarding documentation and CLI setup guidance, with existing CLI report tests updated where needed. Workflow implementation and secret provisioning are separate:

- https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/issues/61
- https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/issues/100

Do not add runtime label selection, make GitWeave read Project state, implement cancellation or merge gates, change resource limits, or automatically edit target repositories during init.

## Acceptance / validation

- A new operator can follow the guidance from Project initialization to label-driven Ready synchronization and `projectweave coordinate`.
- README, usage guide, and init report consistently distinguish manual and automatic onboarding and describe the agreed transitions without contradicting one another.
- Validate relevant init-report tests if the CLI report changes. Documentation and tests must not require live GitHub mutations, credentials, or AI execution.

## References

- https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/automating-projects-using-actions
- https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/adding-items-automatically
